136: ✦Your baby is 17–19 cm long, about the size of a banana.✦It weighs about 300 grams.
137: ✦In girls the uterus keeps developing; in boys the testicles begin moving down from the abdomen.✦It will take a few months for the testicles to fully descend into the scrotum.
138: ✦Your baby spends part of the time sleeping.✦Sleep can last from 20 minutes to 2 hours.✦Although they can move their eyes left and right, the eyelids are still closed.✦As thin layers of fat form under the skin, the skin is getting thicker.✦So your baby keeps gaining weight.
139: ✦The baby's skin is covered with a layer of fine hair called lanugo.✦This hair starts to disappear after 36 weeks.✦Very little remains after birth.✦What's left falls out within a few months.
140: ✦The vernix caseosa layer on the skin, which started forming last week and will decrease over time, keeps increasing this week.✦This fatty substance contains 40–50 different proteins.✦Vernix protects the baby against various infections in the womb and in the days after birth.✦It also protects the baby's skin from the acidity of the amniotic fluid.✦This thick, creamy coating also makes it easier for the baby to pass through the birth canal.
141: ✦This week your baby will taste whatever you eat and start getting used to – and liking – those flavours.✦That's because the amniotic fluid tastes different every day depending on what you eat (hot pepper one day, banana the next), and your baby now swallows this fluid daily (to stay hydrated, get nourishment and practise swallowing and digesting).
142: ✦Your baby is now about 26 cm long and weighs 310 g.✦As hearing develops, they can hear you talking, singing and laughing.✦Your baby's organs can now absorb small amounts of sugar from the fluid they swallow.✦This sugar reaches the intestines and leaves the body as waste.✦The kidneys can now process waste more efficiently.
143: ✦The baby's digestive system will start absorbing energy-giving nutrients from the amniotic fluid they swallow.✦But most of the baby's nutritional needs are still met by the placenta.
144: ✦The skin is now fully covered with vernix caseosa.✦Most of this thick, paste-like protective coating, important for the immune system, disappears before birth.
145: ✦Organ development is largely complete.✦Bone marrow formation is speeding up.✦Your baby's brain keeps growing rapidly, and this growth will continue for at least a few years after birth.
146: ✦The baby's senses keep developing.✦With a developing sense of taste, your baby notices your eating habits.✦If you eat something sweet like chocolate, they may move more.✦They're increasingly aware of light and noise from outside.
147: ✦Thanks to the amniotic fluid, your baby's development continues.✦This fluid protects the baby from bumps.✦By swallowing amniotic fluid, the baby also fills and empties the lungs, practising breathing.✦This prepares them for breathing after birth.✦The fluid also keeps the baby's digestive system working.
148: ✦For a few weeks, stool called meconium has been forming in the intestines.✦The baby will keep storing it in the intestines until birth.✦Normally the baby doesn't pass this stool before birth.
149: ✦This week your baby is about 28–29 cm long, the size of a large zucchini.✦It weighs about 430–450 grams.
150: ✦The lungs keep developing and will start producing a substance (surfactant) that allows breathing after birth.
151: ✦Your baby's thin, pink skin is now covered with vernix.✦The amount of fat under the skin keeps increasing.✦Two distinct skin layers are forming: the outer layer (epidermis) and the deeper layer (dermis).✦The epidermis that will form the prints on the fingers, toes, palms and soles keeps developing.✦There are tiny blood vessels in the lower skin layer.✦On top is the fine hair called lanugo.✦The paste-like vernix covering the skin decreases until birth.✦Babies born early still have a thick layer; babies born late may have less.
152: ✦As brain cells develop and the brain sends signals to nerve endings throughout the body, the senses keep developing.✦This week the sense of touch develops further.✦Reflex movements are giving way to more conscious actions.✦Now your baby touches their face and holds the cord more deliberately!✦These new experiences must make them feel happy.
153: ✦Although for now they only taste amniotic fluid, the sense of taste has fully developed – enough to tell bitter, sweet and sour.✦So your baby may react to your eating habits and the taste of what you eat.✦For example, if you eat something sweet, they may move more.✦Everything you eat passes through the placenta.✦The more vegetables, salads and fruits you eat during pregnancy, the more likely your child is to enjoy them later.
154: ✦The reactions aren't only to taste.✦Your baby can now jump at loud, lively music.✦It's best to play calming music such as classical.✦Slow music like this helps your baby stay calmer.✦The baby can hear their parents' voices.✦If you talk to them a lot, they're very likely to recognise your voice after birth.
155: ✦While red blood cells are being made, a substance called bilirubin is also produced.✦It's filtered by the liver and removed in the urine.✦If it hasn't all been cleared by the day of birth, it can take a few days to leave the body.✦A build-up of bilirubin causes jaundice after birth.✦This usually clears with sunlight and plenty of breastfeeding.
156: ✦Your baby is about 29–30 cm long, the size of a large eggplant.✦It weighs about 500 grams.
157: ✦Your baby's brain cells and senses keep developing.✦With more developed senses, their movements become more deliberate.✦As awareness grows, they're ready for new discoveries in taste, touch and hearing.
158: ✦Communicating with your baby is good for them.✦Recognising your and your partner's voices will help them feel calm when they hear you after birth.
159: ✦Babies can also hear their mother's heartbeat.✦That's why babies placed on their mother's chest after birth often calm down right away.✦Skin-to-skin contact, which keeps mother and baby together after birth, matters for this reason.✦In recent years, mother- and baby-friendly birth practices aim to keep mother and baby together after birth if there's no medical reason not to.✦During this time, skin-to-skin contact and breastfeeding are encouraged.✦Often the second person to hold the baby is the father, introducing the baby to the family's microbes.✦It's said that babies who stay with their mother for the first 45 minutes feel more secure later in life.✦This closeness also strengthens the bond between mother and baby.✦If this matters to you, talk to your doctor about your post-birth preferences and ask for skin-to-skin contact.
160: ✦As your baby keeps swallowing amniotic fluid to practise breathing and keep the digestive system working, the lungs continue to mature.✦The lungs are producing surfactant, which will make breathing possible after birth.✦From next week your baby will reach the stage where they could survive outside the womb with medical help.
161: ✦The fat layer under your baby's skin keeps increasing, but blood vessels are still visible.✦The thick, paste-like fatty layer on the skin called vernix caseosa keeps forming.✦It protects both the baby's warmth and immune system.✦This slippery coating also makes passing through the birth canal easier.
162: ✦The nails and hair keep growing.✦Your baby sleeps in your belly and keeps waking up and moving.✦Your baby's eyes are flickering, but it'll be another 3–4 weeks before the eyelids open and close.
163: ✦Your baby is now about 30 cm long and weighs 600 g.✦They look just like a small baby; proportions are right and the face has formed in full detail.✦The tiny air sacs and blood vessels in the lungs keep developing.✦If your baby were born this week, the lungs would be ready to work with artificial support.
164: ✦Since the development that lets the lungs breathe in the outside world is largely complete, from this week your baby could survive with medical help if born early.✦That's why in the USA a 24-week baby is considered viable.✦In the UK the legal threshold of viability is also set at 24 weeks.
165: ✦Your baby's senses are largely developed.✦As brain cells develop, the baby can respond more consciously and perception has improved.
166: ✦Your baby can hear sounds very well now.✦Play calming music and talk to your baby whenever you can.✦Saying loving, positive words can help them feel good.✦You can even plan the birth together by talking to them.✦If you tell them you'll have a healthy, positive birth together, they'll feel it.✦You may be surprised how such words reflect positively on the birth.
167: ✦The sense of touch is working nicely too.✦For example, if you gently press your belly, your baby may feel it and respond.
168: ✦Your baby's movements keep getting faster.✦There's still plenty of room, so they're busy testing their developing muscles.✦You may feel some of these movements.✦The development of the senses shows in the movements.✦For example, you may notice jumps when they hear loud music, or more movement when you eat something sweet like chocolate.
169: ✦You can see your baby moving on ultrasound.✦The grasping ability is developing well.✦You may see them easily bring their thin fingers to their face and even hold the umbilical cord.
170: ✦Your baby is about 35–36 cm long, the size of a large zucchini.✦It weighs about 670 grams.
171: ✦Your baby has come an incredible way from the size of a poppy seed.✦They're now a little baby whose development is largely complete.
172: ✦Under US law the baby is now considered a person.✦Even if the lungs aren't fully developed yet, there's a chance of survival with medical help.
173: ✦Although fat keeps building up under the skin, the body still looks thin.✦The vernix caseosa layer on the skin keeps helping to control body temperature.
174: ✦Although your baby's skin keeps getting thicker, there are still capillaries near the surface, so the skin looks pink.✦It's also wrinkled.✦The formation of the skin layers (outer epidermis and deeper dermis) is complete.
175: ✦Your baby's heart beats 140–150 times a minute.✦With all the senses working, your baby keeps exploring through them.✦They may react to loud sounds.✦They may relax to calm music.✦The sense of taste develops further.✦When you eat something sweet, they move more.
176: ✦The skull bones are still soft, so the brain can keep growing easily.✦A soft skull is also what helps the baby pass through the birth canal during birth.✦The skull stays soft after birth too.✦It hardens over time.
177: ✦Your baby is about 36–37 cm long, the size of a large squash.✦It weighs about 780 grams.
178: ✦Your baby may sleep for 20 minutes to 2 hours at a time.✦Your baby will have their own sleep–wake pattern.✦If it doesn't match your routine, you may find yourself woken at midnight by kicks.
179: ✦Your baby keeps swallowing amniotic fluid to practise breathing.✦They filter this fluid through the digestive system and pass it as urine.✦This helps increase the amount of amniotic fluid.✦Having enough amniotic fluid is vital for the baby.✦There's now about 500 ml of amniotic fluid.✦It's renewed every 3 hours.
180: ✦The baby's heart rate has slowed compared with the early weeks.✦It beats 140–150 times a minute.✦The outer and deeper skin layers have formed.✦This week the skin starts producing pigment to gain its colour.
181: ✦At the start of this week more hair has grown.✦The hair colour hasn't formed yet.✦Some babies are born bald, others with a full head of hair, some of which falls out.✦Some babies are born with dark hair that lightens within a few months.✦The opposite can happen too: a baby may be born with light hair that darkens within a few months.
182: ✦The nails, eyebrows and eyelashes are being completed.✦Hand and footprints are becoming clearer.✦The whole body is covered with fine hair called lanugo.✦Lanugo supports skin development and keeps the body warm.✦Most of it falls out before birth.✦The rest will fall out within a few months after birth.
183: ✦The vernix caseosa layer (a thick, fatty coating) that has been on the skin for 5–6 weeks will keep controlling body temperature until there's more fat under the skin.✦Although it decreases before birth, some is still on the baby at delivery.✦The remaining vernix also helps the baby pass through the birth canal.
184: ✦Your baby has more taste buds in the mouth now than at birth.✦This means they not only notice what you eat through the amniotic fluid but may react to it.✦For example, some babies respond to spicy food with hiccups.✦Or they may kick when they taste spices.
185: ✦From week 27 the fat under the skin will increase faster.✦Fat is also building up around the organs.✦In the last 3 months of pregnancy your baby will come a long way toward being chubby.✦As fat builds up, the fine hair on the skin (lanugo) will fall out, leaving the job of keeping warm to the fat.
186: ✦As connections between the brain and nerve endings increase, the senses are completing their development.✦Since your baby started opening and closing their eyelids last week, the eyes are more sensitive to light.✦If a bright light shines on your belly, they may squint.
187: ✦The brain – and so the head – keeps growing.✦As signals from the brain to nerve cells increase, the baby moves more consciously.✦Research suggests a primitive memory forms in these weeks.✦Studies also suggest that from this week babies store the language (even a different one) or songs they hear often in their memory.
188: ✦Are you ready for tiny punches and kicks? We can almost hear you say, 'Goodness, what's going on with this baby?'✦Your baby is going through the most active period of the journey in the womb.✦Don't worry that your child will be hyperactive!✦It's far too early to think that.✦Babies move so much because they enjoy exploring their developing senses and there's still plenty of room.✦There's also plenty of amniotic fluid for their acrobatics.
189: ✦Your baby has started making regular breathing movements by swallowing amniotic fluid.✦You may feel these as hiccups and see them on ultrasound.✦Even though they make breathing movements, the placenta still provides all the oxygen the baby needs.
190: ✦As pregnancy progresses, the baby's movement and sleep settle into a pattern.✦There are periods of more or less activity lasting 1–3 hours.✦But if your baby is unusually still and not as active as usual, it's a good idea to talk to your doctor.
